reviews.title: Immersive and Vast
reviews.text: Takes me back to the good old days of text based desktop games (think Oregon Trail set in Feudal Bavaria)….you can try to speed run it or spend a whole day on every turn, wish there were faster ways to reference specific realms/individuals. It can be frustrating when you’re trying to stoke an alliance between your heir and another kingdom, but you keep forgetting who you were courting, etc. overall though, minor gripe. Part of the fun is how primitive and nostalgic it feels

I downloaded this yesterday and haven’t stopped playing since. It’s so incredibly detailed and well thought out. You don’t have to spend money to have fun (but I did buy some gems and the Kingdom scenario which is fun, and I felt the devs deserved my money lol). I love the realism.

My only thing is the game can be confusing sometimes because there’s so much to do. A more in-depth tutorial would be useful! Also, sometimes when I do certain actions like starting a pregnancy it isn’t reported on the diary page and I wish it were.

Anyway this game is so cool, thank you so much!

reviews.title: Imagine if you mixed BitLife and Reigns together
reviews.text: This game is absolutely fantastic, though I do I have a few minor complaints. First off there's certain nations you can't form for reasons I don't fully understand, like Switzerland for example. Second, unless you buy the China or Japan maps (which thankfully you can buy with gems you can save up for by doing daily missions), you're currently limited to just the British Isles, mainland Fr*nce, and the former Holy Roman Empire, and that last one isn't entirely accurate, as some parts, such as most of Northern Italy, Schleswig-Holstein, and Prussia are unfortunately absent as of the time I'm writing this. However that's just it, they are not currently available AS OF THE TIME I'M WRIGHTING THIS, and it wasn't long ago that only the British Isles and mainland Fr*nce were playable on the default map, so I feel confident in asserting that it's only a matter of time until the default map expands yet again, I wouldn't be surprised if the map of China you can buy with gems is also expanded eventually for that matter. Third and finally this game is in many ways very historical, so there's nothing supernatural present like in BitLife or Reigns, but at the same time, your character, or characters in game, can have hair colors, eye colors, and skin tones that aren't strictly historically accurate for the time period I imagine this game takes place. The inaccurate ethnic traits doesn't really bother me much honestly, but I would appreciate an menu option for more accurate ethnic representation, especially if that option came in an update that included Spain, Italy, Corsica, Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia, with Egypt, the Levant, Anatolia, the Balkans, and Scandinavia added eventually as well in addition to the rest of Holy Roman Empire I mentioned earlier, though I doubt anything outside of Europe will be added anytime soon. But all and all, Medieval Life is still the best mobile game I've played in a very, VERY long time, and I highly recommend it, especially if you're looking for a more casual version of something like Crusader Kings 3, in which case, this is pretty much perfect for you.

There’s an error that pops up frequently, stalemating the education progress for all children making you manually click “study hard” for progression in education. It’s quite annoying. If this was fixed, game would be 5 stars.

reviews.title: Fun… BUT
reviews.text:
I really enjoy this game. I love that you can change the success laws of the kingdom, go to war and gain more land through conquest, make alliances and enemies!
I just wish there were a few more things:
We cannot marry into other kingdoms. My king cannot marry the daughter of the French or Scottish king as they would in real life. On that note, I wish there were more kingdoms in the game as well.
I like that characters can die in childhood and childbirth - it makes the game and succession more realistic. I just wish my character’s life didn’t always last 80+ years. Every single one! Maybe add a feature that there’s a chance they die if there’s a war going on? Or natural death accruing starting in their 50s? Because my unplayed heirs have the chance of dying at any time which makes it harder to move on. 
:)
